2. Filter patients with known tissue_prospective_collection flag (YES vs NO).
3. Aggregate expression to patient level.
4. Perform principal component analysis (PCA) on the expression matrix (centered and scaled).
5. Plot PC1 vs PC2, coloring points by prospective vs retrospective.
6. Test for difference in PC1 scores between groups via t-test.
7. Identify top genes contributing to PC1 (highest absolute loadings).

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# 1. Load clinical data
df_clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
# Filter patients with known prospective collection flag
df_clin = df_clin[df_clin['tissue_prospective_collection'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]
# Map patient -> collection method
clin_flag = df_clin.set_index('bcr_patient_barcode')['tissue_prospective_collection']

# 2. Load gene expression data
df_expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)
# Transpose: samples x genes
expr_T = df_expr.T
# Extract patient IDs (first 12 chars)
expr_T['patient_id'] = expr_T.index.str.slice(0, 12)
# Keep only patients in clinical
expr_filt = expr_T[expr_T['patient_id'].isin(clin_flag.index)].copy()
# 3. Aggregate expression to patient-level (mean across samples)
expr_pat = expr_filt.drop(columns='patient_id').groupby(expr_filt['patient_id']).mean()
# Align labels
groups = clin_flag.loc[expr_pat.index]

# 4. Standardize and PCA
scaler = StandardScaler(with_mean=True, with_std=True)
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(expr_pat)
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)

# Prepare DataFrame for plotting
df_pca = pd.DataFrame(X_pca, index=expr_pat.index, columns=['PC1', 'PC2'])
df_pca['collection'] = groups.values

# 5. Plot PC1 vs PC2 colored by collection method
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.scatterplot(data=df_pca, x='PC1', y='PC2', hue='collection', s=50)
plt.title('PCA of Gene Expression by Tissue Collection Method')
plt.xlabel('PC1')
plt.ylabel('PC2')
plt.legend(title='Prospective Collection')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 6. T-test on PC1 scores between groups
pc1_yes = df_pca.loc[df_pca['collection']=='YES', 'PC1']
pc1_no  = df_pca.loc[df_pca['collection']=='NO',  'PC1']
t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(pc1_yes, pc1_no, equal_var=False)
print(f"T-test on PC1: t-statistic = {t_stat:.3f}, p-value = {p_value:.3e}")

# 7. Top 20 genes by absolute loadings on PC1
loadings = pd.Series(pca.components_[0], index=expr_pat.columns)
top20 = loadings.abs().sort_values(ascending=False).head(20).index
top20_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'gene': top20,
    'loading': loadings.loc[top20]
}).reset_index(drop=True)
print("\nTop 20 genes by absolute PC1 loading:")
print(top20_df.to_string(index=False))

Hypothesis: Prospective vs retrospective tissue collection methods introduce systematic shifts in baseline tumor transcriptome profiles.

Experiment results:
- After filtering for patients with known prospective collection flags (YES vs NO) and averaging sample‐level expression to patient‐level, PCA was performed on the centered and scaled gene expression matrix.

These results provide strong evidence of a batch‐like effect associated with tissue collection method, as patients with prospective versus retrospective collection exhibit significantly different transcriptome profiles along the primary axis of variation (PC1).

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Patient‐level somatic mutation burden is positively correlated with Breslow tumor thickness at diagnosis.

experiment_plan.objective: Quantify the relationship between total somatic mutation count per patient and Breslow thickness to test if higher mutation burden associates with deeper tumors.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Load cleaned_mutations.csv and cleaned_clinical_data.csv.
2. For each patient_id, count total somatic mutations (all Variant_Classification) to define mutation_burden.
3. Extract Breslow thickness (breslow_thickness) from clinical data; filter out missing values for either variable.
4. Merge mutation_burden with breslow_thickness by patient_id.
5. Compute Spearman’s rank correlation and fit a simple linear regression (breslow_thickness ~ mutation_burden).
6. Create a scatter plot of mutation_burden vs Breslow thickness with regression line and 95% confidence interval.
7. Report statistical parameters: Spearman’s rho, p‐value, regression slope, intercept, R².
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Table of patient_id, mutation_burden, breslow_thickness
• Spearman correlation coefficient and p‐value
• Linear regression model summary (coefficients, R², p‐values)
• Scatter plot with regression line and confidence band
• Short interpretation of the relationship between mutation burden and tumor thickness

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Patients harboring activating BRAF V600 mutations exhibit elevated expression of key MAPK‐pathway genes at baseline.

experiment_plan.objective: Assess differential expression of MAPK‐pathway genes between patients with BRAF V600 mutations and those without.

2. Identify patients with any HGVSp_Short containing "V600" in the Hugo_Symbol 'BRAF' rows; label these as BRAF_mutant, others as BRAF_wild.
3. Aggregate expression data to patient‐level (average across samples per patient).

• Summary interpretation of pathway activation differences

untried_experiments.hypothesis: High baseline expression of MUC16 is associated with reduced overall survival in melanoma patients.
